tasks.short: Prepare technical reports and experimental charts

steps.what: Select experimental results and specify report tables and chart variables
Prepare graphs, charts and result tables in the report format
Write technical interpretation, check charts and release the final report

tasks.design: Configure repeatable table and chart templates in {SPREADSHEET} and {DOCS}, or the native laboratory information system {OTHER}. The technician selects and checks results, writes interpretation and verifies the exact report before release; chart generation does not choose exclusions or scientific conclusions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated chart formatting and table placement can require manual assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reporting templates can repeat a specified layout over checked results.
tasks.still_hard: Units, excluded observations and axis choices can change the apparent meaning.
tasks.human_edge: The technician distinguishes reliable experimental findings from artifacts and overinterpretation.
tasks.altitude: Less chart assembly, with experimental interpretation and report responsibility unchanged.

reach.task: Check result traceability in a technical report
reach.learn: Method versions, units and correction history

evidence.claim: LabWare LIMS generates certificates of analysis with signatures and audit trails; this supports native laboratory report generation, not this experimental-report time estimate.
Template charts for experimental reports and the savings scenario are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is technical report preparation, excluding conducting experiments and original result measurement.

In s1 the technician produces sample/run ID, method version, result value, unit, replicate, qualifier, inclusion decision, chart variable, axis and display limits. All 45 hours remain, including capture and checking. Missing or inconsistent data returns to manual report preparation.
Test native laboratory reporting and workbook charts before custom code. No model infers scientific conclusions or invents absent results.
Allow five focal hours for template repair and unusual-result reconciliation beyond routine report checks.
research_questions: Do template charts reproduce independently checked values, units and exclusions without misleading axes?

already_counted.description: Data selection and scientific report checking

approvals.approved_version: Exact report, charts, source dataset version, units and inclusion decisions; changes require another technician check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus5 upkeep =20 net. High assumes repeated manual chart assembly; low covers already-native reports or atypical experiments. Interpretation remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inventory laboratory materials and order supplies

steps.what: Inventory laboratory materials and verify usable quantities and expiry
Choose needed materials, quantities and supplier items
Populate the materials order request from selected purchase lines
Check the request and submit it through existing purchasing controls

tasks.design: Use native catalogue-to-request copying in {PROCUREMENT} after the technician has counted stock and selected exact purchase lines. The technician checks and submits the request; stock assessment, material suitability and downstream purchasing approval remain unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected catalogue items may be retyped into a separate request form.
tasks.enabler_now: Native requisition functions can populate exact selected item fields.
tasks.still_hard: Chemical grade, pack size, usable stock and planned demand require human checks.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises when a nominally similar material is unsuitable.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate request entry; material and quantity decisions remain with the technician.

reach.task: Resolve a chemical item or pack-size query

evidence.claim: Native request population from selected catalogue lines is an E1 design from model knowledge; the digest supplies no laboratory supply-order case.

assumptions: Boundary is technician inventory and requisition preparation, not supplier fulfilment or purchasing-team approval.

In s1 the technician produces item/lot, location, usable quantity, unit and expiry; all 40 hours remain. In s2 the technician captures supplier item ID, grade, pack size, quantity, price, cost centre and verified delivery location; all 30 hours remain. Missing fields require manual entry and checking.
No free par level, reorder flag or structured address is assumed. Test native catalogue selection before code and claim s3 savings only where a second entry exists today.
Allow four focal hours for catalogue mismatch and request-form upkeep beyond routine checks; no new purchasing-team curation is transferred.
research_questions: Can selected lines populate the request without losing grade, pack size or delivery details?

already_counted.description: Stock capture, material selection and request check

approvals.approved_version: Exact purchase request version, item specifications, quantities, cost centre and delivery location; changes require another technician check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gross20 minus4 upkeep =16 net. High needs repeated entry after counted stock and purchase-line capture; low covers already-native requisitions. Physical inventory retains time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct or monitor chemical production workers

steps.what: Direct or monitor workers producing chemical products and address deviations

tasks.design: Retain direct observation, instruction and intervention. Existing instructions in {DOCS} support supervision; no model monitors worker behaviour or issues production commands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe supervision depends on actual activity and process context.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems do not establish equivalent worker supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected practices and process conditions require immediate contextual response.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices misunderstanding and intervenes within their authority.
tasks.altitude: Supervisory responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Keeping chemical-production supervision human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's supervision, not the workers' production time.
No structured worker-performance flag or machine action is assumed.
Existing instructions remain; no custom monitoring system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
research_questions: Which observed deviations require immediate intervention versus supervisory escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Human supervision retains all time and outside worker labour is excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Design experimental apparatus around the research question and operating constraints
Fabricate apparatus and check its physical function before experimental use

tasks.design: Retain experimental design judgement and physical fabrication. Requirements in {DOCS} guide construction; a generated sketch does not establish safe materials, performance or fitness for use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Novel apparatus must satisfy physical and experimental constraints together.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting capability does not replace construction and validation.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected interactions and practical tolerances emerge during fabrication and testing.
tasks.human_edge: The technician adapts the design to observed physical behaviour and seeks qualified review.
tasks.altitude: Apparatus design and fabrication responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify apparatus performance and construction constraints

evidence.claim: Keeping novel apparatus design and physical fabrication human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's design and fabrication work, excluding the full research project.

Between s1 and s2 existing laboratory authority and qualified engineering or safety reviewers authorise the design under current practice. Their unchanged work is outside the focal baseline; no new transfer or automatic approval is proposed.
No free structured engineering requirements or machine-generated safe design is assumed. Existing design documents and workshop tools remain.
Zero incremental upkeep because this workflow does not change.
unknowns: Apparatus complexity and required review arrangements
research_questions: Which requirements need qualified engineering review before physical construction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Design, fabrication and physical checking retain time; no hypothetical drawing-copying share is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeat report assembly and request re-entry where observed while preserving chemical judgement, inventory checks, supervision and apparatus work.
reach: Resolve report traceability with quality analysts
Clarify apparatus constraints with laboratory engineers
role.ambitious_version: A chemical technician who produces traceable reports and supply requests while keeping attention on actual laboratory and production conditions.
